ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, what is the solid represented by its net?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} According to the unfolded figure, there are a total of 5 faces, with two triangles serving as the base and three rectangles as the lateral faces,\\
$\therefore$ this solid is a \boxed{triangular prism}.

ready2_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, what is the solid represented by its net?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the diagram, what is the solid represented by its net?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a plane net; in the middle, a triangular region is enclosed by dashed lines; outside the three sides of this triangle are respectively connected three quadrilateral side faces, among which the lower one is a rectangle, and the left/right upper ones are inclined rectangular or parallelogram side faces; outside one side face on the right is also connected another triangular end face. Reasoning: When folded, the two triangles will become the two congruent bases above and below or front and back, and the three quadrilaterals will enclose the side faces connecting the two triangles. A solid that has two congruent triangular bases and three rectangular side faces is a triangular prism.

raw_record.question_text: As shown in the diagram, what is the solid represented by its net?

method.method_draft: Inspect the diagram as a net: identify a central triangular region indicated by three dashed fold lines, three rectangular/parallelogram side panels attached along its three sides, and another congruent triangular end face attached to one of the rectangular panels. Read the question text as asking which 3D solid is formed by folding this net. Use the rule that a prism net has two congruent polygonal bases and rectangular lateral faces; since the bases are triangles and there are three rectangular side faces, the solid is a triangular prism.
